5.10 Challenges and Future Directions in AI-Driven Technical Analysis

There are some challenges of applying AI in Technical Analysis which are briefly explained in this section.

103.

5.10.1 Challenges in AI-Driven Technical Analysis

5.10.1.1 Data Quality and Availability

The quality and availability of data is the primary challenge in AI-driven technical analysis. To identify patterns and to make predictions, AI algorithms rely on large datasets. Financial markets produce vast amounts of noisy, incomplete, or unstructured data (Cao et al. 2020).

  • Noisy Data: massive quantities of price data, trading volumes, and other variables are generated by the financial market. This data contains noise, random, irrelevant fluctuations, which can lead AI models to draw incorrect conclusions. AI systems may overfit the noise instead of identifying meaningful patterns if not properly handled.
  • Limited Access to Alternative Data: AI models are enhanced through alternative data sources such as social media sentiment, satellite imagery, or credit card transactions, but accessing such data can be expensive and may require partnership with specialized data providers.
  • Historical Bias: Data that may not always reflect future market conditions are used for training AI models. Due to shifts in macroeconomic policies, geopolitical events, or technological advancements, market dynamics change over time, resulting in the struggle of models that are trained on past data to predict future trends accurately.

5.10.1.2 Overfitting and Generalization

The risk of overfitting where models perform well on historical data but fail to generalize to new market conditions is another significant challenge in AI-driven technical analysis.

  • Overfitting to Historical Data: AI models may become too specialized, capturing noise and irrelevant details that do not apply to future market movements when AI models are trained on a specific set of historical data. When applied to real-time trading, overfitted models can lead to poor performance and significant losses.
  • Dynamic Market Conditions: By changing investor sentiment, economic conditions, and external events financial markets have become highly dynamic. Those models that were effective in one market environment might not generalize well to new conditions. Let us consider the case where a model trained on data from a bull market struggles to perform well in a bear market.

5.10.1.3 Model Interpretability

Interpretability has become a significant challenge for traders as AI models have become more complex. It is becoming difficult to understand how AI models arrive at certain predictions, particularly those using AI techniques such as deep learning or ensemble methods, which are often referred to as black boxes.

  • 104. Regulatory Implications: Regulators require that trading decisions made by algorithms must be auditable in the financial industry. Concerns over compliance with regulations in cases where AI models are responsible for executing high-risk trades can raise due to lack of transparency in some models.
  • Lack of Transparency: When it comes to risk management, traders understand the logic behind trading decisions. It becomes hard to explain why a certain trade was executed or why a particular trend was predicted due to lack of transparency of AI models.

5.10.1.4 Ethical Concerns and Market Manipulation

Concerns over the ethical implications of automated decision-making by AI-driven trading in financial markets are as follows:

  • Market Manipulation: Markets can be manipulated either intentionally or unintentionally by advanced AI systems. For example, algorithms that are designed to exploit small inefficiencies in a market could contribute to flash crashes and can cause rapid price swings by overwhelming order books.
  • Fair Competition: There is a concern that AI-driven trading could create an unfair competitive environment as larger institutions have access to better AI technology and more comprehensive datasets. With more sophisticated models and higher computational power, smaller firms may struggle to compete against larger institutions.

5.10.1.5 Computational Costs and Infrastructure

Computational power and infrastructure to process vast amounts of data and execute trades in real time are required in AI-driven technical analysis.

  • High Computational Requirements: Powerful hardware such as graphical processing units or cloud-based infrastructure is required for training and deploying AI models, especially deep learning algorithms. Difficulties might be faced by smaller traders and firms accessing or maintaining such resources.
  • Latency in Execution: The latency involved in processing data and executing trades can lead to missed opportunities in high-frequency trading, where milliseconds matter. AI models may introduce delays that rely on large datasets, and complex computations may reduce their effectiveness in fast-moving markets.

5.10.2 Future Directions in AI-Driven Technical Analysis

Exciting possibilities for trading have been offered by the future of AI in technical analysis despite the challenges. Many of the existing challenges are likely to be addressed by innovations in AI technology, data migration, data integration and model explain ability resulting in unlocking new opportunities for AI-driven trading strategies.

105.

5.10.2.1 Explainable AI (XAI)

XAI focuses on making AI models more interpretable and transparent for human users and will be the future of AI-driven technical analysis.

  • Regulatory Compliance: Ensuring compliance with financial regulations is also a crucial role of XAI. XAI techniques will help traders provide the necessary audit trials and justifications for trading decisions as regulators demand more accountability from AI systems.
  • Improved Interpretability: Traders can understand how AI models reach their conclusions, improving trust and usability through XAI techniques. Simplifying complex models or developing new algorithms will offer a higher degree of transparency without sacrificing predictive power.

5.10.2.2 Improvement in Data Integration and Processing

Traders can use a broader range of datasets to enhance AI models by advancement in data integration and processing capabilities.

  • Real-Time Data Analytics: AI models will become more effective at analyzing intraday data with the growth of IoT technologies and real-time data collection resulting in improving accuracy of short-term predictions and helping traders capitalize on fleeting opportunities.
  • Alternative Data: Traders will increasingly turn to alternative data sources, such as social media sentiment, environmental data, or real-time corporate data as the demand for more predictive power increases. There will be a competitive edge in predicting market trends with an AI model that can seamlessly integrate traditional financial data with alternative data.

5.10.2.3 Hybrid Models Combining AI with Human Expertise

The combination of AI with human expertise will likely become a dominant strategy although AI has been proved to be a powerful tool for technical analysis.

  • Blending AI and Fundamental Analysis: To create more robust trading strategies AI models could be combined with fundamental analysis in addition to technical analysis. Traders can make more informed decisions that account for both technical and economic factors by incorporating fundamental data such as earnings reports, economic indicators, or corporate news.
  • Human-in-the-Loop Models: Human judgment into the decision-making process can be incorporated by future AI systems allowing traders to validate AI-generated insights. Traders can apply their market experience to improve AI predictions by this “human-in-the-loop” approach.

5.10.2.4 Quantum Computing in AI-Driven Trading

AI-driven technical analysis is revolutionizing quantum computing, leading to faster computations and enabling the generation of more complex models.

  • 106. Optimizing Complex Portfolios: Traders optimize complex portfolios more efficiently by solving optimization problems that are too difficult for classical computers through optimizing complex portfolios. Integrating AI models with quantum computing could provide unprecedented precision in portfolio management.
  • Enhanced Computational Power: Traders will be able to run more sophisticated AI algorithms on larger datasets in real time as quantum computing becomes more accessible resulting in the improvement of the ability to predict market trends, especially in high-frequency trading or multi-asset portfolios.

5.10.2.5 AI-Enhanced Risk Management Tools

A stronger emphasis will be placed on risk management in the future of AI-driven technical analysis, helping traders to mitigate risk in real time.

  • Real-Time Risk Analytics: AI models will continue to be enhanced which offer more sophisticated risk management tools that can dynamically adjust trading strategies based on market conditions. For example, stop-loss levels, hedge positions, or adjust portfolio allocations based on real-time market volatility can be optimized through AI.
  • Predictive Risk Models: Forecasting market downturns or sudden volatility can be improved using AI, helping traders implement defensive strategies ahead of time. AI can reduce exposure to adverse price movements by identifying early warning signs such as anomalies in market behaviors or shifts in sentiment.

5.11 Conclusion

Tools and techniques have been provided by AI-enhanced analysis to improve risk management in technical analysis for traders. AI helps traders mitigate risks and optimize their trading strategies by leveraging pattern recognition, predictive indicators, dynamic stop-loss strategies, and real-time risk monitoring. The robustness of risk management frameworks has been enhanced by the integration of sentiment analysis, anomaly detection, and portfolio management ensuring that traders are well prepared for various market conditions. Traders hold enormous potential for optimizing trading strategies, improving risk management, and generating superior returns through the integration of AI into technical analysis. However, traders must navigate challenges such as data quality, model interpretability, overfitting, and ethical concerns. The future of AI-driven technical analysis will be shaped through innovations in data integration, XAI, hybrid models, enhanced risk management, and quantum computing. Traders can unlock the full potential of AI in navigating the complexities of financial markets by overcoming these challenges and embracing new opportunities.

6 Future Trends and Ethical Considerations in AI, ML, and IoT

Sarabjeet Kaur, Swarnima, Purnima Pal, and Nidhi Sharma

DOI: 10.1201/9781003561873-6

6.1 Introduction

The idea of linking sensors or “things” anywhere, at any time, is known as the Internet of Things (IoT). Through the connection of tangible items, it expands the reach of the Internet into the real world; this phenomenon is commonly referred to as a “ubiquitous network” or “cyber-physical system.” Innovations in network protocols, embedded systems, and microelectronics will play a major role in the future development of IoT [1]. An outline of the many industries that IoT may change in the upcoming years is given in this chapter. It looks at how driving on national highways might change in the future, how common apparel might change from being just fabric to something more, how important two-way communication will be in future power grids, and how IoT is helping to conserve threatened species like rhinos [2]. It also looks at the difficulties IoT developers encounter and how data safety will affect IoT networks in the future. A summary of several business models that manufacturers might use as IoT devices proliferate in the market is provided in the chapter’s conclusion [3].

6.2 Applications of IoT

IoT applications are numerous and have grown significantly in the last several years, and this will be covered in more detail in the following sections. It’s critical that developers go beyond fundamental cloud programming fundamentals to expedite the creation of these applications. A solution that interfaces with cloud application programming interfaces from technologies like Aneka has been proposed as a framework to address this problem [4]. This system may collect information from online databases and sensors, and it can send out messages in response to the detection of particular occurrences of interest.

Figure 6.1 shows an overview of the design [5].

  • Physical Object: This describes a material object that directly helps the user, such as a light bulb.
110.
  • Sensor/Actuator: A small computer outfitted both sensors and actuators is located in the first layer. The actuator reacts by acting in response to the data collected by the sensors about the thing being monitored or its surroundings. For instance, an actuator may decide to turn on or off the lightbulb in response to sensor data indicating the presence of a person.
  • Connectivity: The subsequent layer gives users anywhere access to the World Wide Web.
  • Analytics: This component gathers and keeps track of sensor data while confirming its accuracy.
  • Digital Service: The last layer arranges the previous levels’ digital services in a format that is readily available.

Because each layer is displayed in a different colour, they are all visually different. To design an IoT application, the structure suggests a hierarchical relationship in which every component builds upon the one behind it.

6.2.1 Intelligent Transportation

IoT principles are anticipated to be used in cars soon, establishing networks that facilitate the transfer of high-speed multimedia data for entertainment. Vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANETs) are networks that facilitate device-to-device (D2D) 111. communication. With D2D, devices may find each other and interact directly with little assistance from the network. This can help lower latency, especially when it comes to vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication. Within a 100–300 metre radius, automobiles function as wireless routers or nodes to form a network with other cars [6–8]. Vehicles are cut off from the network as soon as they travel outside of this range. Considerable progress has already been made in the development of intelligent transportation networks. Global companies have developed tools to help volunteers collect roadway data for mapping, which benefits both users and authority (street bump), made parking easier with sensor technology (Park Sight), and made it possible for customers to hail transportation with one mobile device tap (Uber) [9]. It is expected that IoT will significantly influence how drivers interact with their environment, especially traffic. The many communication techniques that VANETs are anticipated to use are shown in Figure 6.2.

6.2.2 Smart Clothing

At present, only specialised, low-volume textiles with electronic components are suitable for making smart clothing. Future IoT applications for clothing, nevertheless, are anticipated to incorporate sensor layers – like conductive coatings or conductive thread meshes – during the production phase. For this, three essential conditions have been specified in detail:

The variables that the sensor layers are intended to identify and the precise body locations that they are intended to monitor require customisation.

For the sensors to receive power and be able to communicate, there needs to be connectivity between their levels.

To integrate clothing with electronic circuitry, an interface must be used.

The electrically controlled modules may also include a specific operating system along with the functionalities previously mentioned. IoT may also be used for quality control and product inspection [10]. For instance, a clothing hanging design has been developed that evaluates the clothing’s tensile durability and capacity to endure continuous use in addition to examining its appearance, including colour and fit, to make sure it satisfies predetermined standards [11].

Researchers are also exploring how to create a sensor system that would optimise the heating or cooling of a building based on occupant clothing insulation. The goal of this strategy is to stop energy waste and lessen pain from high or low temperatures. In order to compute the residents’ clothing insulation, the Smart Sensor Systems for Clothing Insulation Inference (SiCILIA) collects environmental and personal data [12].

6.2.3 Smart Grids

Smart metres could only measure how much electricity was consumed and remotely turn on or off the power source as necessary in the past. But when IoT concepts are incorporated into more advanced electrical networks, smart metres should be able to 112. 113. do an increased number of tasks. These new features include the capacity to capture activities such as equipment status and power quality, integrate with different services like water and gas, and track utilisation of energy in real time with options for both nearby and distant metre readings [13].

Important elements:

Electronic Control Unit (ECU) and Sensors: Cars come with sensors (shown by blue dots) and an ECU (represented by a red dot) that monitor driving characteristics and communicate with the surrounding infrastructures.

Network Infrastructure:

Cellular base stations (BS): Offers wireless communication coverage throughout the road network.

Wi-Fi access points (AP): Provides on-road infrastructure and automobiles with local connectivity.

Road Infrastructure: To improve safety and better manage traffic, features including parking services, speed control structures, and traffic lights are combined.

Communication from Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X):

Vehicles can exchange location and speed information with one another through V2V communication.

Vehicles and road infrastructure, such as traffic signals or signs, exchange data using Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) communication.

Vehicle-to-Road (V2R): Information about conditions such as speed restrictions or warnings is sent to vehicles via the road infrastructure.

Vehicles communicate with external sensors to receive real-time traffic information via Vehicle-to-Sensor (V2S) communication.

Range of Wireless Access Infrastructure: The footprint shows how far wireless communication may reach, spanning cities and guaranteeing constant vehicle contact.

Services:

Speed control uses communication with the path infrastructure to track and regulate the speed of the vehicle.

Parking Services: Provides up-to-date information on parking spots that are available.

Traffic Information: Gives drivers the most recent information on traffic patterns and directions.

The goal of this interconnected system is to facilitate the advancement of autonomous driving technology while also optimising traffic flow and safety.

To establish a secure connection, the smart metre – which is believed to be information collection device – could be connected to a device that communicates like an intelligent gateway. It’s essential to remember this. This entrance might obtain and share information in real time from the provider and even turn on and off the power source [14].

Furthermore, by connecting to home appliances, this gateway might send consumption statistics to the next generation of the electrical grid. By directly transmitting voltage and current readings to a central aggregating point, smart metres are expected to eventually substitute the many sensors now used in the grid and save expenses [15].

For transferring this data within a smart grid’s neighbourhood area network (NAN), several communication strategies have been investigated. To collaboratively convey information from an initial node to a node of destination through multiple relays, one study, for instance, developed an experiment bed using software-defined radios (SDRs) [16]. This configuration was tested in both indoor and outdoor environments, demonstrating that increasing the quantity of relays improved reach distance while maintaining a comparable level of service (QoS) and increased network energy savings when compared to systems that did not use cooperative interaction [17].

One of the research results is shown in Figure 6.3, which supports the conclusion that increasing the number of relays to maintain the same quality of service can lengthen the network’s lifespan. Given that most devices in the IoT system are powered by batteries, this is especially critical [18].

Furthermore, it creates a media access control, or MAC, protocol specifically for these kinds of networks. One set of the authors’ results is shown in Figure 6.4.

The throughput variation to boost source-destination (SD) lengths at various transmit powers for cooperative and single-input single-output (SISO) lines is depicted in the image. Plotting shows that a network that cooperates with a source broadcast strength of 5 dBm can achieve a throughput efficiency comparable to a SISO system with a broadcast strength of 10 dBm. This is a significant finding.

6.2.4 Education

Since Internet access is so widely available, learners and investigators are more eager than ever to connect with peers and subject matter experts. The World Wide Web is becoming a crucial medium for exchanging concepts and continuing research. Experts from a range of fields are expected to be asked to give lectures via live video streaming in the future. Global education has greatly improved since massively open course offerings (MOOCs) were introduced. With top colleges increasingly providing open access to their faculty, the “flipped classroom” idea has become more popular. With this approach, teachers may concentrate on addressing issues and concepts in class because students are required to study the content outside of the classroom [19]. Students in countries that are developing, whose access to higher learning can be hindered by monetary limitations, now have an opportunity to pursue learning 114. beyond the basics through MOOCs and other online assets like the Khan Academy. Both homebound keen learners and those who cannot pay for college tuition may find their quality of life enhanced through this access.

Plotting shows that throughout a range of relay numbers and distances, LOS communications (light gray surface) achieve a longer network lifespan than NLOS communication (dark gray surface).

MOOCs have the potential to develop into two-way communication platforms in the future, providing schools and teachers involved in these projects with useful data. Datasets about registration numbers, rates of abandonment, online attendance, and IP addresses of students can be generated by MOOCs. Universities will be enabled to use this data to determine the amount of time students spend studying and to pinpoint subjects and content that appeal to particular groups of people. Consequently, educators might enhance their pedagogical approaches to minimise attrition and customise syllabuses according to the requirements of learners.

6.2.5 Tracking, Predicting, and Safeguarding the Environment

Considering the continuous strain that extensive urbanisation and harmful human behaviours like sport hunting are placing on the planet, it is anticipated that IoT will have a major role in preserving biodiversity and endangered species. Organisations across the world are using GPS-enabled devices to track the behaviour and health of these animals to protect them. Cisco, for instance, uses long-range (LoRa) radio connection to track people’s movements as they look at rhino reserve regions. Safety 115. measures can be undertaken to protect the animals’ health and safety in the event of trespassing [20].

The graph shows that throughput decreases with increasing distance for both power levels and that cooperative communication continuously outperforms SISO in terms of throughput. Furthermore, for both communication techniques, higher power (10 dBm) results in better throughput performance than 5 dBm.

In addition, IoT can help solve problems with waste disposal, especially in the United States of America, where the average daily weight of trash produced per person was 4.6 kilogrammes in 2013. IoT can assist with tackling issues associated with waste buildup in communities by determining the best times for garbage removal and the most effective routes for collecting trucks to take. Another major environmental concern is forest loss, for which Bio Carbon Engineering is replanting a billion trees, one endeavour that is incorporating drone technology. Using drones to survey deforested areas and precision agriculture methods that cut expenses and labour, this organisation hopes to accomplish its goals. Finally, IoT can be extremely helpful in anticipating and lessening the effects of natural disasters. For example, Zizmo uses sensors connected to the cloud to identify activity close to seismic epicentres and alert nearby next-door neighbours. It is possible to develop comparable technology to improve response and preparedness for disasters. In a similar vein, Avatech forecasts the chance of an avalanche using pressure sensors.

116.

6.2.6 Smart Agriculture and Farming

The world’s water reservoirs are quickly running out, as has been demonstrated, making it imperative to protect this essential resource. According to estimates, farmers utilise 70% of the freshwater on Earth, 60% of which is lost because of water-intensive crop cultivation, inadequate irrigation infrastructure, and unproductive agricultural techniques.

Sensors along with actuators can help growers see more clearly into their operations and minimise wastewater by keeping an eye on important parameters including water pressure and temperature. For example, Macrostrain has created a wireless sensor system that is intended to evaluate critical conditions in vineyards during the growth season. By monitoring elements like soil moisture, temperature, and solar radiation, these devices notify farmers of harsh circumstances that could have an effect on the wellness of their crops. Figure 6.5 outlines the potential uses of IoT in agriculture.

6.2.7 Health Care

It should come as no surprise that IoT is expected to transform health care as well, given its plethora of potential uses. Doctors may now keep an ongoing eye on their patients’ physiological signs owing to IoT. Recent advances in embedded systems and wireless sensor networks, or WSNs, have made miniaturised monitoring of health devices possible. Together, these sensors can create a system of body sensors (BSN), which monitors health markers and enhances responsiveness through context-aware sensing.

One common application for BSNs is the monitoring of ongoing electrocardiogram (ECG) signals for the evaluation of cardiac disorders. Furthermore, compared to evaluations based only on clinical observation, these WSNs have shown to be successful in tracking individuals with Parkinson’s disease since they offer dependable data gathered over prolonged moments in time. For instance, wearable sensors have been used by researchers to assess Parkinson’s patients’ movement patterns, enabling highly accurate real-time surveillance. BSNs are useful in the treatment of respiratory conditions too. To assess the amount and pace of breathing in this case, the network is equipped with respiratory devices. The information gathered can help those who need breathing exercises, which prove essential for respiratory disease rehabilitation. Using respiratory sensors, the device helps patients breathe correctly, which is essential to their healing.

6.2.8 Smart Homes/Buildings and Monitoring

In homes, sensors can be quite helpful in preventing any potential health hazards. Environmental sensors, for instance, can keep an eye on a number of variables, including temperature, humidity, hydrogen sulphide concentrations, quantities of carbon monoxide gas leaks, and air quality shown in Figure 6.6. Users can obtain these details from remote locations owing to startups like Netatmo. Some companies have implemented IoT ideas to domestic lighting and air quality monitoring. Meethue, for example, provides mobile device-controlled smart bulbs that adjust to the weather, preferences of users, time of week, and the activity within the room. 117. In addition, certain technologies for smart homes have been created to help older people. Ubi, for example, is a voice-activated laptop that offers voice memos, podcasts and a sound calendar in addition to lighting-based notifications that highlight particular events. Building security has also been improved using IoT technologies. Some entrepreneurs have created sensors for lift and boiler maintenance, as well as sensors that can be placed on structure foundation for continuous load monitoring. In addition, if a fire extinguisher fails to appear in its assigned spot or if its pressure falls below safe operating limits, users can receive alerts from distant fire extinguisher tracking systems.

Drones for Field Surveillance (top): Providing real-time data for aiding decision-making, drones help monitor crop circumstances and field health.

Water Management (right): Accurate monitoring and automated watering are two ways that IoT-powered devices maximise water consumption.

Soil factors such as humidity and nutrient levels are measured using sensors (bottom) that allow for better crop growth management.

Routine Operational Machines (left): Daily farming activities are automated by IoT-integrated gear, increasing productivity and lowering labour requirements.

The main theme is agriculture IoT, which illustrates how IoT is transforming agricultural methods.

118.

6.2.9 Public Safety

Device-to-device (D2D) connectivity is one method that IoT might improve public safety. Multi-hop interaction among sources and destinations is made possible by broad device installation, and this is especially helpful in times of crisis. As the majority of those electronics run on batteries, energy efficiency must be given top priority in any network built for such types of scenarios.

Following a calamity, a lot of gadgets can be broken and incapable of facilitating communication. Additionally, owners of portable electronics might disable external control, which could hinder communication. Communication blocking is not an option in disaster and terrorist scenarios due to the sensitive nature of content. As a result, in an emergency, the network needs to be robust and able to reorganise itself.

Furthermore, low battery power may cause a number of nodes to stop transmitting data. The likelihood that information will arrive at its intended location increases if nodes have the ability to autonomously adjust transmission protocols. In such cases, 119. a “disaster mode” may be engaged, which would use specific routing for low-power communications and prevent pointless D2D contact. In addition, IoT is now a vital tool for effectively managing crowds. Authorities can monitor crowd movements, assess any safety risks, and make prompt choices to ensure public safety during major events or emergencies using real-time data gathered via sensors.

6.3 Research Challenges

Although IoT has opened many interesting prospects for further development, researchers continue to fight with hurdles inhibiting its progress. This section will seek to define some of these issues.

6.3.1 Versatile Sensors and Technologies

The first issue is handling a large number of diverse nodes for sensors, which makes connections to the Internet of networks of sensors highly complex and diverse. With numerous networks using diverse communications techniques, IoT systems generally lack a consistent framework for seamless device identification and branding. In addition, due to the enormous volume of data transferred, these systems typically experience delays and other transmission problems. One of the main areas of ongoing research is creating network protocols that guarantee the smooth transfer of data from multiple sensing devices in IoT-enabled systems. IoT networks also benefit from modularity, which lets users design their own effective objects independent of a single vendor’s offerings.

6.3.2 Integration of IoT and Conventional IT

To create a single information structure, IoT must also be integrated with traditional information technology (IT) platforms. The creation of middleware would also be necessary for the integration of IoT devices with current software platforms. Additionally, an IoT network’s sensors generate a lot of real-time data which may not be immediately relevant to the final user. The end-users will have to possess significant big data abilities to make use of the available information, which might prove extremely difficult in itself.

6.3.3 Standardisation

Standardisation is another issue that needs to be addressed to improve the interoperability of different applications and, in turn, performance as a whole. The future standards for the IoT should facilitate a smooth transfer of information between various types of sensors manufactured by manufacturers across the globe. They should also address security and radio access issues and industry-specific modifications to meet the specific needs of various sectors.

6.3.4 Security Protocols

The growth of strong security mechanisms to protect privacy is one of the fundamental components of IoT standardisation. IoT networks are susceptible to hackers 120. since they depend on cloud servers. The strict requirements of some industrial applications might not be fully met by the information security mechanisms in IoT systems today. Compared to wireless sensor networks (WSNs), the challenge of developing encryption algorithms for IoT networks is bigger because IoT systems connect a large number of commonplace devices that gradually gather large volumes of private data. For example, safe interaction will be essential in the years to come for self-driving cars that use VANETs to avoid nefarious activity that could result in hazardous scenarios like incorrect information causing collisions. Similar to this, robust security protocols are required in the healthcare sector for body sensor networks (BSNs) to protect patient privacy when transmitting medical data to doctors shown in Figure 6.7.

121.

6.4 Business Models

A business plan for bringing in money and turning a profit from its operations is called a business model. Because of the character of the IoT ecosystem, businesses have to collaborate with both competitors and companies in other industries. As a result, traditional business models are inapplicable to the IoT phenomena.

The vast number of devices connected inside these networks, the necessity of incorporating recent IoT innovations into useful items and offerings, and the uncertainty surrounding stakeholder roles, organisation, and governance in this rapidly growing area are some of the current IoT difficulties. Many frameworks for IoT business models have been investigated in the literature. “Design Needs Goals” (DNA) represents such a model. In this paradigm, the “Needs” refers to the relationships with consumers, “Goals” refers to the desired results like making money, and “Design” refers to the vital components of the structure, such as resources and activities.

One unique element of IoT services is their capacity to track user behaviours and feedback over time, which lets companies add new features to their products. This fits the definition of a business model which is service-dominant.

In addition, the model can be used for efficient process optimisation and forecasting. Unlike traditional models where firms create value alone, under this service-based business strategy, customers and companies work together as collaborators in value creation. Table 6.1 delineates the essential components and obstacles of a service-based model that builds upon the network-centric perspective in IoT business.

Furthermore, there are six primary components to another IoT-specific company structure known as digitally charged goods. These elements include ideas like physical free of charge, which offers a tangible product in addition to a free digital service, 122. such as maintenance or installation guides. With digital add-ons, consumers can purchase additional services from the original seller or other sources in addition to what the good provides. A sensor-based electronic verification procedure known as “digital lock-in” guards against fake goods and upholds guarantees.

6.5 Major Key Issues and Challenges of IoT

Substantial complexity is added due to the prevalence of Internet connectivity for various systems in every facet of human lives and various techniques involved in data transfer among embedded devices. IoT developers have several problems and difficulties to deal with, especially as society adopts more sophisticated smart technology. The difficulties and demand for more advanced IoT systems also grow as technology evolves. IoT developers should cultivate foresight by anticipating new problems and proactively collaborate to generate creative solutions to address them.

6.5.1 IoT Ethical Concerns

The biggest problem facing businesses is that consumers don’t fully comprehend how their IoT goods operate when they use them. In addition, it is widely believed that IoT security is woefully inadequate and highly vulnerable to cyberattacks. According to a Forbes study, the number of cyberattacks using IoT devices has increased by 300% in 2019 [21]. This was due to rapidly rising number of gadgets and an absence of emphasis on safety rather than creativity.

123.

6.6 AI and ML

The design and development of sophisticated computer systems that can carry out tasks that normally require human intelligence is known as artificial intelligence (AI). Speech recognition, visual perception, making choices, language comprehension, translation, and independent problem-solving constitute a few of these activities. AI systems are becoming more and more capable of adapting, learning, and functioning on their own, which makes them adaptable to a range of settings. To be able to go through data, gain insights from it, and use this knowledge to carry out duties effectively, technological businesses are developing software and hardware that uses AI [22, 23]. Organisations are investing significantly in AI, from chatbot and quantum computing to driverless cars, to boost productivity and produce faster and more accurate results than with traditional human-driven approaches.

6.6.1 New Developments in AI

6.6.1.1 Siri

One of Apple’s most well-known assistant programs Siri is accessible on the majority of their electronic products, including the iPad and phone. Individuals commonly engage with the female controlled by voice help at any time. When it comes to finding information, getting directions, making calls, sending texts, launching apps, and planning events, she is essential.

6.6.1.2 The Tesla

Cars have grown in popularity as AI targets. Those who are interested in cars are missing out on Tesla. It is arguably the most popular vehicle on the market. The car has won many awards and is known for its self-driving capabilities, predictive abilities, and cutting-edge technological innovation.

6.6.1.3 Cogito

Cogito, one of the best examples of the behavioural version to increase the intellect of customer service personnel, was co-founded by Dr. Sandy and Joshua and is currently available for purchase. The company uses behavioural science and ML to enhance phone experts’ customer participation. Every day, countless voice calls may use Cogito. AI technology tracks human speech and provides immediate feedback to help individuals behave better.

6.6.1.4 Echo

Amazon released Echo, which now has additional features and is smarter. It is a cutting-edge solution that provides Alexa, a voice service to assist you with checking the web for personal data, arranging appointments, making decisions, navigating, switching, and heating and cooling systems, answering questions, reading Audible, reporting traffic and weather, giving you information about nearby businesses, offering sports schedules and ratings, and more. The remainder of the chapter covers the uses of AI and a few of its possible advantages.

124.

6.6.2 Business Applications of AI and ML: Present Uses and Upcoming Prospects

The way businesses analyse data and decide is being transformed by the growing integration of AI and ML. Businesses utilise such tools to improve client relations, streamline repetitive operations, and perform statistical analysis. Businesses may optimise operations like managing stock, service delivery, and advertising efforts by using algorithms that use ML to find undetected patterns in large datasets. A major shift in business methods is exemplified by the trend towards data-driven decision-making, which is changing sectors such as manufacturing, banking, and retail [24]. The potential of AI and ML in business is bright. The use of NLP to improve customer interactions and the expansion of AI-powered targeted marketing solutions are examples of recent advancements. As ML models advance, businesses will give responsible AI practices more thought, guaranteeing data transparency and dependability. Additionally, these tools will become more widely available owing to advanced ML frameworks, allowing smaller businesses to employ AI or levelling the playing field [25].

6.6.3 The Significance of Ethical AI

  • Influence on Society: The widespread use of ML (AI) systems and their significant social influence cannot be emphasised. They have the power to fundamentally shift the economy, modify political environments, and change cultural norms. Such transformative potential necessitates a corresponding dedication to ethical supervision of AI since its unchecked development may have unexpected repercussions and disproportionately affect those with limited resources.
  • Conscientious Innovation: Ethical AI is a prerequisite for responsible innovation and serves as a moral guide. The idea of “dual use” technological advances draws attention to the fact that AI has the capacity to be a tool that may be applied both positively and negatively [26]. Through ethical innovation, we hope to optimise AI’s potential benefits while minimising any potential downsides.

6.6.4 Frameworks and Principles of Ethics

  • Fairness: A fundamental ethical value in AI is fairness, which requires AI to treat every person equally. However, achieving fairness is a challenging endeavour that is hampered by issues concerning algorithmic bias, data gathering, and the establishment of fairness criteria. Since algorithmic equity aims to address the deeply ingrained biases found in many AI systems, it demands thorough evaluation.
  • Explainability and Transparency: Both of these are essential components of AI ethics. The black-box nature of deep learning models needs more research because opaque AI systems have the potential to erode trust and 125. responsibility. Therefore, in addition to becoming morally obligatory, seeking model clearness and transparency is essential for promoting the broader adoption of AI.
  • Accountability: In the context of AI, accountability includes both criminal responsibility and an ethical duty to fix the harm caused by AI. Demonstrating duty in thinking is a difficult task since artificially intelligent systems behave in a distributed style. Two moral frameworks that provide useful perspectives on AI accountability are consequentialism and deontology.
  • Security of information and privacy: Privacy, a basic human right, presents significant ethical challenges in the age of AI. The way AI systems gather, retain, and use data raises complicated questions about knowledge, anonymisation, and information protection. With the aid of legislation like the General Privacy Regulation (GDPR), significant attempts have been made to protect the privacy of individuals in AI applications.

6.6.5 AI and ML’s Ethical Challenges

  • Discrimination and Bias: AI bias presents a significant ethical issue. This bias may be derived from historical data, which might then embed prejudices from culture into algorithms and result in adverse effects. These issues occur in a number of situations, such as hiring decisions, justice systems, and lending practices. Ethical considerations have to solve systemic injustices.
  • Economic Impact and Employment Displacement: The ethical implications of AI have an impact on the economy as well, specifically in terms of employment displacement. AI-driven automation raises questions about society’s responsibility to displaced workers and puts certain job sectors at risk. Widespread retraining programs and universal basic income (UBI) are two ethical strategies for reducing these effects.
  • Autonomous Decision-Making: The growing use of AI in autonomous decision-making, such as in medical diagnosis or driverless cars, raises difficult ethical questions. As demonstrated by the “trolley conundrum” in robot cars and the ethical dilemmas presented by AI in hospitals, it is imperative that we set ethical boundaries for AI’s autonomous choices. The urge to align AI’s ideas with our own lies at the heart of these difficulties.

6.7 Future Trends in AI, ML, and IoT

  • Integration of Edge Technology: To analyse data faster and make judgements instantly, use edge computing rather than cloud-centric processing. Use local data processing to reduce latency and improve privacy.
  • Explainable AI, or XAI: XAI is the development of open AI models to increase trust and responsibility. Verify if ML algorithms are understandable.
  • 126. Federated Learning: ML that collaborates without sharing raw data among scattered devices, promoting security and privacy while improving model accuracy.
  • 5G Convergence with IoT: Greater connectivity that enables smooth communication between IoT devices is known as 5G convergence with IoT. It facilitates real-time data sharing and supports innovative applications like self-driving vehicles and smart cities.
  • AI-Powered IoT Automation: AI integration for proactive maintenance in IoT devices, self-healing networks, and workflow automation.
  • Blockchain-Based IoT Safety: Blockchain technology is used to ensure data integrity and safeguard IoT, making IoT ecosystems more transparent and trustworthy.
  • Blockchain-Driven IoT Security: IoT is protected and data consistency is guaranteed through the use of blockchain technology, increasing the transparency and reliability of IoT ecosystems.
  • Conscientious IoT and AI Ethics: To address social concerns, there is a growing emphasis on creating AI in a moral way and implementing IoT devices sensibly.

6.8 Conclusion

By creating new opportunities for interaction, automation, and decision-making, IoT, deep learning (ML), and AI are revolutionising different sectors. Themes including edge computing, learning federation, XAI, and IoT-5G integration are influencing these technologies’ future. However, their quick acceptance also raises significant ethical concerns about privacy, algorithmic bias, safety hazards, and environmental preservation. To solve these problems, policymakers, technological professionals, and users must take a proactive and collaborative stance. Open administration, user-focused designs, and ethical frameworks are essential for ensuring that technological advancements align with social values. Finding a balance between innovation and moral responsibility will enable the creation of systems that are hospitable, safe, and sustainable. By encouraging multidisciplinary cooperation and transparency, AI, ML, and IoT may realise all their capabilities and offer revolutionary benefits while upholding the interests of individuals and communities globally.

7 Voice Assisted Chat Bots in Enhancing CRM in Modern Marketing for Small Businesses

Aditi Srivastava, Ajay Singh, and Brij Mohan Singh

DOI: 10.1201/9781003561873-7

7.1 Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have completely changed the digital world and brought about real, observable improvements that have increased the effectiveness of the digital world. Presently dominating the market, AI and ML are predicted to transform the sector radically in the coming year [1]. The introduction of voice assistant chatbots has made the expansion of small businesses via digital marketing efforts even more noticeable [2]. Any marketing strategy that focuses on how businesses deftly and successfully maintain long-term relationships with their consumers and persuade them to make future purchases must include customer relationships as a key component [3]. Customer relationship management (CRM) is a crucial component of business and indicates consumer loyalty when they are pleased with the offering. Having strong and long-lasting relationships with consumers is essential to defining CRM since it persuades them to make additional purchases and creates space for future success in sales. CRM is monitored by systems; nowadays, AI and ML are used to monitor them. Fuzzy data technology has been used in AI and ML for advancements in research [4]. These two technologies allow for greater fusion and excellent service when they are used for operation and promotion. Small businesses have first-mover advantage benefits if they can adopt advanced AI-enabled chatbots on their websites [5].

Understanding consumer preferences and choices for Internet services and features has become more crucial for marketers thanks to the Internet [6]. The usage of technology has increased the population of the technology market in 2023 (technologies and 2021, 123AD). Over 5.4 million people used technology to accomplish their tasks in 2023 as per Internet World Stats (2020) (statistics (itu. int)). Technology is a must in the digital age to live. People may now socialize, remain in touch, and have easy access owing to technology. It is hard for us to envision our lives without technology. Our lives are now more dependable and easier owing to technology. Since technology has emerged as an essential tool, it is vital to know how consumers use it daily and how confident they feel when using online platforms. People in the digital 130. age have ready access to technology. Introducing these technologies has resulted in a significant shift in customer engagement. Technology has enabled people to select from a wide variety of products available and select at their convenience in the long run. Good technology-driven platforms are likely to attract more people by promoting engagement. The tech-savvy behaviour of users even motivates them to purchase beyond their basic needs. A customer’s comfort level with technology has a significant impact on their behavior, especially in the context of customer experience (CE). It’s critical that using technology to improve work be accepted. Various models like the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), and the Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) are considered the most effective theories and help study technology’s influence on customers [7, 8, 9].

In the digital age, it is essential to comprehend and adjust to technology. Technology has enabled people and businesses to evolve and develop strategies to sustain themselves in the market as per the advancements [10, 11]. Many clients avoid using online platforms despite their ease of use and lack of cost because they are afraid of technology or have a phobia of it. It is essential to ascertain if people utilize technology freely and how confident they feel after doing so. The likelihood of being back to the same platform for repurchases is increased by the confidence gained via online shopping. In the digital realm, a platform that exudes confidence and dependability is highly valued. The analyst focuses on how to retain customers and ensure they return to the same platform. Platforms which are driven by customization are preferred over platforms which lack customization. Technology has even enabled users to customize their purchase behaviour as per their needs and requirements.

Social media platforms provide greater viability for small businesses and e-commerce platforms to carry out businesses in the long run. The wide reach has enabled businesses to focus on social media platforms for making purchase decisions. Different models have been developed over time to study how technology plays a vital role in making purchases on e-commerce platforms. Customers’ purchasing habits have been dramatically altered by the early adoption of the TAM and the adoption of the UTAUT model.

AI and ML are tools used to analyze consumer engagement and expectations on e-commerce platforms. This study utilizes the UTAUT model adopted from the three most famous theories: TAM, TPB, and TRA [12]. Previous research has concentrated on various UTAUT models and technology model extensions from various angles. Every study has concentrated on the customers’ perception of technology, how easily it has made consumers tech-savvy, and how it has encouraged them to use it more frequently. It is even more important to understand how technology and digital platforms play a vital role in influencing and persuading the shopping behaviours and experience of customers for electronic products.

Small business firms have seen a great hike in sales in recent years; therefore, it is critical to see how technology and its acceptance are important for purchase on e-commerce platforms for this study. Given how frequently technology is used in all spheres of life and how well it raises our spirits when performing our duties, we must comprehend the technology acceptance model. One must be able to use technology freely and perceive its benefits to accept it. After using technology, the performance increases and the procedure becomes much simpler. Technology-enabled tasks are 131. preferred, and they boost the confidence of the user. This saves the time of the users. They feel more confident and tech-savvy after using these platforms.

The AI-enabled chatbot model highlights the fact that a great platform with an effective and efficient system is necessary to facilitate the purchase and repurchase of products from that platform [13]. A more efficient platform ensures less complexity and more output-based performance, especially when consumers do not want to spend more time navigating between pages in a confused state [14]. The present research is significant and to a great extent contributes to the existing research by focusing on the small business product segment which has seen a rise in demand and sales over the decade because of the increased use of social platforms. Social influencer marketing popularly known as (SIM) has led development and growth of social media promoting cost-effectiveness. An increase in demand and change in trends every quarter motivate the present generation to shop more small business products. Good discounts and festivity seasons promote more sales on such platforms; therefore, it is essential to know the digital platform and have good knowledge of latest technologies. The research gap focuses on how much customers feel comfortable using technology to buy small business products, leading to more customer engagement.

This study evolves around the research questions to be answered to enable the industry to understand the behaviour of consumers. It is vital to understand because Gen Z is even more impulsive and wants the platform to be hustle-free for quick navigation. They are as follows:

  • RQ1. What is the applicability of the UTAUT model in today’s digital era for small business products?
  • RQ2. How effectively can the model encode the voice-based chatbots (VAC) responsible for adapting the e-commerce platform’s usability and efficiency?

In the upcoming sections, we will delve into an extensive literature review, present the framework, and outline the methodology adopted in this study. By doing so, we aspire to give a robust foundation for determining and interpreting intricate dynamics at play in the realm of voice-assisted chatbots (VAC) for e-commerce applications for small business product purchases. This is essential in industries, as such an analysis provides a greater understanding and broader perspective of businesses. The framework provides space for improvement and better strategies to support and help with business extensions.

Here, the primary focus is on studying the significance of the UTAUT model and how VAC can affect the buying behaviour for small business products. The study uses VAC as a moderator to bridge a research gap in the latest literature available [15]. The literature lacks the contribution of VAC as a moderator and how VAC moderates the buying behaviour in e-commerce platforms for electronic products. The literature highlights the use of AI, and its applications lead to better customer engagement. Advanced levels of chatbots enable better performance and enhanced customer satisfaction [16]. Chatbots are in use now and customers are repeatedly using them to interact and solve their queries of purchase. Chatbot voice assistants play an essential role in small businesses where brands need recognition and more customer engagement to promote their goodwill in the market. Small businesses need recognition and 132. growth. They need customer engagement and desire to retain customers in the long run. A delighted customer is more like a family to customers. Chatbots enable 24/7 customer support, and they enable more customization for customers. The purpose here is to investigate the following objectives:

  1. To determine and understand the applicability of AI and its enhanced use in small businesses, such as voice chatbots.
  2. To study the association of all the factors used in the UTAUT model in determining CE in electronic products in e-commerce platforms.
  3. To study the moderating role of VAC and its effects on all constructs in the UTAUT model.

7.2 UTAUT Model and Its Elements

The UTAUT theory is one of the most predominant and effective among the eight theories on technology and innovation because it has simplified and enhanced the whole construct into four main elements and four moderating factors that affect customers [17]. The UTAUT theory ought to be the most appropriate for understanding the behaviour of consumers and how they adopt technology in their behaviour [18]. The UTAUT model comprises the most researched constructs and has produced the most significant results recently [19, 20, 21]. UTAUT is identified as potentially persuading people’s CEs to be tech-savvy [21]. The elements are specifically identified to study the customers’ behaviour and how they react to technology [15, 22]. This theory has used three elements: performance expectancy, effort expectancy, and social influence (SI) as influencing factors in determining the CE of users [23, 24]. Experience and gender cannot be taken in this study since they have already been applied to other studies [25, 26]. The EE and PE constructs have a more significant effect on CE in the fintech industry as per the literature [27]. The four constructs have also been tested successfully in learning and management systems and show their substantial associations in the model [12]. Technology-friendly customers are more likely to use technology [6, 28, 29, 30] and online platforms than less tech-savvy customers (Im et al., 2011) [31]. To understand the behaviour, the UTAUT model is popularly adopted to study customer psychology [13, 17, 23, 32]. The UTAUT model comprises four constructs that are used in this study and are discussed below. Popular literature focuses on these constructs to study the behaviour of customers in using technology [28] and the extent to which customers feel friendly in using these technology-driven platforms [31, 33–36].

7.2.1 PE and CE

PE is termed as the frequency to which a consumer believes that employing tech will enable them to perform more efficiently, hence strengthening their belief in using technology. The author has also found that among the factors, PE is the strongest and most important construct influencing the behaviour and usage of technology [37].

  • H1: PE considerably affects the CE in e-commerce apps for small business products.
133.

7.2.2 EE and CE

EE is the frequency to which a user finds using tech to be simpler [38–40]. When discussing many industries, such as health care and mobile uptake, it is regarded as a crucial component [41, 42].

  • H2: EE directly affects the CE in e-commerce applications for small business products (Rahi et al.) [28].

7.2.3 SI and CE

At present, SI is considered essential since it compels individuals to adjust to contemporary technologies [43]. Everywhere, people embrace and value tech-savvy users on a social level, and vice versa [44]. People are frequently compelled by society and social pressure to adopt newer technologies, and they do so frequently [39]. SI has a significant impact on users because of the digital era (Lu, Yao, and Yu, 2005) [36]. Different sectors like health care have seen significant effects of SI on users [39, 42].

  • H3: SI significantly affects the CE in e-commerce apps for small business products.

7.2.4 FC and CE

FC has a direct and substantial influence on users’ CEs and intentions for using technology.

H4: FC significantly affects the CE in e-commerce apps for small business products [45].

7.2.5 CE and CRM

In numerous fields where CE is found to be a strong predictor of consumer behaviour utilizing technology, numerous studies have placed a strong emphasis on CE and CRM [46].

  • H5: CE of users considerably impacts the CE that motivates users to adapt e-commerce applications for small business products [47].

7.2. 6 Voice-Assisted Chatbots and Customer Engagement

VAC in AI are a new concept and enabling such features in platforms for small businesses will promote small businesses and help them have good brand infirmity for customers. There have been many developments in AI using ML to promote websites [48]. VAC provide better CE and provide larger exposure to customers to engage in websites more precisely. They are guided by chatbots very effectively and are recommended products that fit the best of their abilities. With emerging AI, VAC are the future of shopping, enhancing the journey of customers through a new lens.

134.

7.3 Research Methodology

The chapter focuses on how AI will enable customer engagement using the UTAUT model in small businesses. The UTAUT model is adopted to know the applicability of AI in online websites. UTAUT is a very famous research model for studying and understanding customer perspectives and how customer engagement is created for small business models. The study uses AI-enabled voice assistants like chatbots and their enhanced uses to gain customer engagement. The chapter is empirical and includes framing of a questionnaire to be filled by people who are actively using small businesses for their shopping needs. The data is collected using an online Google form. Purposive sampling was used in the study because only those respondents who purchased from small businesses were contacted as shown in Figure 7.1. The sample size of data collection was approximately 690 and SEM was used in the study to understand customer engagement using AI-enabled VAC shown in Figure 7.2. The questionnaire was divided into two sections where the first section included the demographic profile of the respondent and the second section included information on AI-enabled voice assistants used in purchases from small businesses. Chatbots are more trustworthy and enable the building of goodwill and trust for companies [49].

7.3.1 Instrument Development

The items of the questionnaire were constructed using previous works of literature and they were modified. There were two sections in the questionnaire. To create scales for the use of PE, EE, SI, FC, and CE, the original items from Ref. [40] were changed and fitted to e-commerce. The experience was also gauged by how frequently e-commerce mobile applications were used. The academic professionals with relevant experience were shown the questionnaire’s final iteration. Their input had a vital role in enhancing the clarity of the questionnaire. In the second section, there were two stages in which the data was collected. The primary stage of the study consisted of questions that demonstrated the moderating role of the four constructs of the UTAUT model and the mediating variable CE to purchase. The first stage focused on how the moderator variable VAC moderates the association between the IV and CE as a moderator. The first stage also utilized demographic profiling of the respondents, such as age, gender, and occupation, and was gathered in the first part. The questions were framed using the 5-point Likert scale, which ranged from 1 being “strongly disagree” to 5 being “strongly agree.”

135.

7.3.2 Data Analysis

We used partial least squares (PLS) regression to analyze the offered research framework, just like the original UTAUT investigations [38] did. The PLS, created by Herman World in the 1960s, is a practical exploratory analysis tool and likely the least constricting of the multiple linear regression extension [50]. It is beneficial for building predictive models where there may be collinearity among factors. Literature on PLS regression’s benefits and drawbacks can be found [51]. Factor loadings, composite reliability, and average variance extracted (AVE) were used to evaluate the convergent validities, as recommended by Refs [34, 52], while the discriminant validity was assessed by determining whether or not the square root of AVE exceeded the correlation between constructs, as recommended by Ref. [38], and the reliability was assessed by evaluating internal consistency reliability.

7.3.3 Measurement Model

In this stage of the PLS-SEM approach, the measurement model is used to ensure the degree and rationality of the study, confirming their reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity. Using Cronbach’s alpha and composite reliability, the internal consistency and reliability of the construct measurements were assessed [53–57]. As displayed in Table 7.1, all Cronbach’s alpha and composite reliability values exceeded the acceptable threshold of 0.70, as suggested by Ref. [58], confirming the robustness and reliability of all measures.

Following the guidelines outlined by Ref. [59], convergent validity was assessed by examining the standardized factor loadings and AVE. To establish convergent validity, it was necessary to ensure that (i) all measurement items exceeded a threshold of 0.70, (ii) the composite reliability was above 0.70, and (iii) AVE was greater than 0.50 [59, 60]. This study met all these criteria, as indicated in Table 7.2. Consequently, the findings strongly confirmed its convergent validity.

To establish discriminant validity, an assessment was performed by comparing the square roots of AVE with the correlations among constructs to confirm that each factor was distinct or uncorrelated [61–66]. As shown in Table 7.2, all shared variances among factors within the model were lower than the square root of the AVE, indicating dissimilarity between the constructs. The findings revealed a lack of substantial correlation among variables in the model, affirming the absence of multicollinearity in the study, which is consistent with the observations of Ref. [60].

7.3.4 Structural Model and Hypotheses Testing

The second step in the PLS-SEM methodology involves evaluating the structural model. This evaluation analyzes the standardized beta coefficients and t-values associated with the model’s hypotheses. Independent variables, including social media influencer attractiveness, social media platform reputation, and content appeal, were studied in the model. Moreover, informational social influence and normative social influence intention were considered mediators, and impulsive buying behaviour was the dependent variable within the model.

Hypothesis H1 determined whether PE considerably affects the usage of voice-assisted chatbots. The relation is positive here. The results presented in Table 7.3 revealed that performance expectancy played a substantial role in predicting the usage of VAC within this context (β = 0.37, p < 0.05), confirming hypothesis H1. Hypothesis H2 examined whether EE positively affects the usage of voice-assisted chatbots. Table 7.3 demonstrates that effort expectancy does have a substantial impact on the use of VAC (β = 0.45, p < 0.05), supporting hypothesis H2.

Hypothesis H3 tested whether SI affects the usage of voice-assisted chatbots. The relation is positive here. According to the results obtained from PLS-SEM, it was determined that SI significantly influenced the usage of VAC, with a β value of 0.34 and a p-value less than 0.05. Consequently, hypothesis H3 was validated. Hypothesis H4 determined whether FC positively affects the usage of voice-assisted chatbots. The outcomes indicated that facilitating conditions played a substantial role in predicting user behaviour, with a β value of 0.24 and a p-value less than 0.05. Therefore, hypothesis H4 was supported. Hypothesis H5 tested whether the use of voice-assisted chatbots positively affects customer engagement. The robustness of the connections between the two factors offered confirmation for this association (β = 0.67, p < 0.05). Therefore, hypothesis H5 is validated.

7.4 Findings

The results show that PE has a significant positive impact on the use of VAC (β = 0.37, p < 0.05). This confirms that users prefer to adopt the chatbot if they assume it to be useful and effective in enhancing their performance, thereby supporting H1.

139. EF has the highest impact on the adoption of VAC, with a β value of 0.45 (p < 0.05). This finding supports H2, indicating that when people find the chatbot easy to use, they are more inclined to adopt it.

The model confirmed that SI considerably affects the usage of VAC (β = 0.34, p < 0.05). Hypothesis H3 was validated, suggesting that people’s usage decisions are affected by social factors, such as peers, instructors, or social norms regarding technology adoption.

FC, as per the model, positively impacts people’s use of the chatbot (β = 0.24, p < 0.05), confirming H4. This demonstrates that the availability of appropriate technical support and environment plays a significant role in encouraging the use of the chatbot.

The study revealed that the use of the VAC significantly enhances customer engagement (β = 0.67, p < 0.05). Hypothesis H5 was validated, indicating a strong association between chatbot usage and increased engagement levels.

7.5 Discussion

The analysis underscores the relevance of various factors in predicting the incorporation of VAC. PE and EE emerged as the vital predictors, which aligns with the principles of the UTAUT model. Users prefer to use the chatbot if they find it as both beneficial to their tasks and highly adaptable to operate. The effective role of SI recommends that peer recommendations, social norms, and faculty endorsements can heavily influence users’ behaviour to incorporate new technologies. This points to the importance of promoting chatbot usage through community and group activities, possibly leveraging word-of-mouth strategies or testimonials from influential peers or instructors. FC also proved to be an essential factor in chatbot adoption, emphasizing the need for institutions to provide adequate resources and support for people to use these tools effectively. Ensuring that people have access to the necessary infrastructure can significantly reduce potential barriers to adoption. Finally, the study confirmed that the use of VAC enhances customer engagement. This highlights the potential of such technologies not only for academic purposes but also for fostering deeper interactions and relationships with people, improving overall customer satisfaction and involvement.

7.6 Conclusion

This chapter focused on how VAC lead to better customer engagement, ultimately leading to a better customer relationship manager for small business products. The study specifically focused on small business products to help them grow and expand exponentially in the long run. Since now small business products are evolving, small businesses need to incorporate AI in their applications with advanced levels of customer engagement tools. Good customer engagement leads to good customization of websites and applications which eventually leads to better customer retention leading to customer relationship building in the long run. Voice-assisted chatbots enable great customer engagement and they automatically guide customers through their purchase journey, leading to better purchase preferences.

140.

7.7 Theoretical and Practical Implications

This chapter aims to seek how AI has again transformed digital marketing and how it is benefiting small businesses in growing globally. Small businesses have evolved as one of the rapidly growing businesses with the advent of the Shark Tank India and Make in India initiatives. Small businesses are growing exponentially and are preferred by the people [67–69]. With the inclusion of an application-based system, which AI drives, it is even more commendable that these businesses have greater opportunities in the market for growth. The emergence of VAC enables consumers to explore the applications more rapidly. VAC enables easier navigation through websites and how these websites retain customers for longer duration in the e-commerce platforms. A long retention strategy in a website enables consumer purchase. A consumer who is likely to stay more on websites is likely to purchase. This is essential for small businesses to maintain greater visibility in the market. Small businesses design their e-commerce websites as per the customers. Customization in the form of VAC enables a more customer-engaged website. A website that has more customer engagement can build CRM. Good customer engagement can build effective customer relationships. Small businesses need effective CRM for long-term sustainability in the market. Therefore, VAC enable customers to interact with the websites of small businesses more effectively, leading to building of brand image for small businesses. VAC enable searching for products more easily. Customers ask chatbots without typing about products they search for. Chatbots are AI-driven applications that analyze customer behaviour on web platforms and recommend the most suitable products with effective pricing in a couple of seconds. Chatbots assist them personally to have better products in their carts. For small businesses, it is essential to have this feature on their platforms to enable a larger customer engagement, resulting in larger audiences who they cater to. Designing smart applications and websites with smart VAC provides a wider shopping perspective. Customers can use them to navigate the website without even typing. The VAC will analyze more aggressively the behaviour of users.

7.8 Limitations and Future Research

The chapter is practical and is based on innovation; however, it also has some limitations, creating a scope for further research. First, the concept is confined to the UTAUT model. Many other theories have also evolved in management guiding. Secondly, convenience sampling is used for data collection since only those respondents who were conveniently available were considered. In future research, this can also be carried out through random sampling where every participant has a chance. Many other factors are also responsible for promoting small business products using AI, ML, and IoT. Thirdly, future research can inculcate location tracking with advanced voice chatbots that can automatically evaluate the customer’s location and recommend the products of small businesses in nearby areas.
